### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**8** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/marketplace/install-local (route, a path literal in installManaged))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/external-datasources.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/marketplace/install-local (route, a path literal in installManaged))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/seed-data.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/marketplace/install-local (route, a path literal in installManaged))_
- `content/docs/deployment/app-dependencies.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/marketplace/install-local (route, a path literal in installManaged))_
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/marketplace/install-local (route, a path literal in installManaged))_
- `content/docs/deployment/install-modes.mdx`  _(via installMode (symbol, a field of interface InstalledBuild), /api/v1/marketplace/install-local (route, a path literal in installManaged))_

- `content/docs/deployment/publish-and-preview.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/marketplace/install-local (route, a path literal in installManaged))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/marketplace/install-local (route, a path literal in installManaged))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-4.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/marketplace/install-local (route, a path literal in installManaged))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab4419881fc0d7ef2c56304f7aa51f39fd16267c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a71ca680ef333a02ea177dcc0d1e749b3cbbc0c9` — the merge of head `18bbea25a3cceb203ccab9f999884def0fff6e47` into base `ab4419881fc0d7ef2c56304f7aa51f39fd16267c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a71ca680ef333a02ea177dcc0d1e749b3cbbc0c9 && git checkout a71ca680ef333a02ea177dcc0d1e749b3cbbc0c9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ab4419881fc0d7ef2c56304f7aa51f39fd16267c 18bbea25a3cceb203ccab9f999884def0fff6e47 && git checkout -B drift-repro ab4419881fc0d7ef2c56304f7aa51f39fd16267c && git merge --no-ff 18bbea25a3cceb203ccab9f999884def0fff6e47

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab4419881fc0d7ef2c56304f7aa51f39fd16267c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ab4419881fc0d7ef2c56304f7aa51f39fd16267c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T16:15Z

Head-sha: 18bbea25a3cceb203ccab9f999884def0fff6e47
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34687 (second follow-up: the ask-mode install, route A as the seat chose; os-dev report 6953599115).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** Draft, base `main`, `Part of #34687`, with no closing verb. That is right, because the five-repetition round is still owed on the card and re-runs once this lands. Three commits.

**Scope.** Six paths, all inside `packages/qa/scenarios` plus one changeset:
- `src/runner/app.ts` (`installManaged` on `HttpApp`, optional on `AppHarness`, and the door table line);
- `src/runner/orchestrate.ts` (`withInstalledBuild`'s `managedFallback`, `fallsBackToManaged`, `InstalledBuild` / `InstallAnswer`, `installableManifest(…, mode)`);
- `test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts` (one new top-level describe in the runner's shared harness file) and `test/runner/units.test.ts` (one pin);
- the README mode table row;
- `.changeset/34687-ask-managed-install.md`.

No platform path moves: the door, the refusal and its code stay `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s. `PR-body guards` (claim, Part-of) is green.

**Declaration.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body and the changeset, and they agree. Every item listed is reachable from `./runner` and is additive: an optional method, an optional parameter with the old default, three new exports, and two optional fields on `ModeRun.template`. `@objectstack/scenarios` at `patch` is the level `none` takes. A published-type widening owes the seat an L2 at TIER_DEFAULT, as the body says.

**Governed / size.** `check-governed-merges --pr 34911`: NOT governed, 309 lines.

**Check-runs at 18bbea25, read at about 16:15Z.** 48 runs, none failed. `Test Core (1/10)`, `(2/10)` and `(3/10)` are still `in_progress`, so the aggregate `Test Core` has not posted yet. Everything else is `success` or `skipped`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, Test Core shards 4 to 6, `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`. This ACCEPT holds on the condition that the open shards and `Test Core` finish green on this head, which o3-F confirms before landing.

**The fallback, against the platform.**
- Only `UNMANAGED_INSTALL_UNCOPYABLE` falls back, and only in ask mode (`managedFallback` is passed by `askMode` alone). The door's own refusal names the managed install as the remedy, and ask mode edits nothing, so taking it measures the same build.
- The managed body is `installableManifest(artifact, 'managed')`: the unmanaged body minus only the `installModes: ['unmanaged']` the runner adds. I checked the default on this head: `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts:483` reads an absent `installModes` as `DEFAULT_INSTALL_MODES`, and `:665` names that default `['managed']`. So the door reads the build's own declaration. A build that declares `installModes: ['unmanaged']` only would be refused managed too, and that lands in the "both refused" finding. Case 1 pins the body equality and that `capabilities` is kept.
- Every fresh copy installs the way the run's own install landed (`landed`), and never calls the refused door again. Pinned.
- Template mode never falls back. Its agent edits the installed copy, which only an unmanaged install makes the environment's own. Pinned by case 4, and the second ablation (the template guard removed) turns exactly that case red.
- A harness without `installManaged` keeps the refusal as its finding and says why. Pinned.

**The record.** `template.installMode` is now on every install, template mode included. `unmanagedRefusal` is present only after a fallback. `install` is the answer of the install the mode ran on. The readers of `ModeRun.template` on this head (`cli.ts:370`, `scorecard.ts:673`, `summary.ts:264`) read only `source`, so none is changed by the new fields or by `install` now meaning the managed answer after a fallback. The fallback is also listed as an ask finding, and `scorecard.ts` renders findings as lines, not as a failure.

**Error-code provenance.** Comparing the code inline, not declaring it as a runner constant, keeps `check:error-code-provenance` from reading the runner as a stamp site. The docblock names the owner. That is right.

**Live proof.** travel_expense from the pinned template `b7ab31a7`, one repetition: the managed install answered 200, 13 question turns and 6 operations ran, where the refused round ran 0. The seed reaching 173 of 757 matches the scratch run of the same build (the build's own paid-claim rule refuses the inserts), so it is not the install's doing.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1. `summary.ts` does not surface `installMode`. A round summary that sets an ask run from before this PR (unmanaged, or 0 turns) beside one after it cannot tell from the table alone that the install changed. The record and the finding line carry it, and the five-rep round runs all after this lands, so nothing mixes now. If ask rounds from both sides of this PR are ever compared, a column or footnote is the place. Not owed.
- N2. The body's last line is a plain-text signature, not the HTML comment. `PR-body guards` reads it as green, so it is a style deviation only.
- N3. A run of a capability-gated build now carries the same ask finding in every repetition. That is informative, not noise, but whoever reads the five-rep round should know that a finding on those cards does not mean something went wrong.

Next: the seat's L2 at TIER_DEFAULT (published-type widening on `./runner`). o3-F lands after the L2 and once `Test Core` is green on 18bbea25. A later push owes an L1-c delta read.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `18bbea25a3cceb203ccab9f999884def0fff6e47`
Local-runs: none

What I read: card #34687 (the body and all comments, including the 15:01Z claim note that routes option A and the 16:08Z os-dev-report for this PR); PR #34911 (the body and its 6 files); the net diff against merge base `fc5913e1`; and the check-runs on the head. I also read code outside the diff, without reviewing it, to judge the claims: `summary.ts`, `scorecard.ts`, `runner/index.ts`, the install-local door in `cloud-connection`, the refusal in `metadata-protocol` and the spec error-code ledger.

Gates (check-runs on the head): all 49 runs have finished: 33 success, 16 skipped by their own `if:` rules, 0 failure. The green runs include Build Core, Test Core (the aggregate and shards 1–6/10), TypeScript Type Check, all four Type Check lanes, Lint & Repo Gates and every Lint lane, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI and Test UI.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public surface, `./runner`** (`src/runner/index.ts` re-exports `app.js` and `orchestrate.js` with `export *`):

- **`AppHarness.installManaged?`** — a new optional interface member: RIGHT. A harness written before this PR still satisfies `AppHarness`. The test case "a harness with no managed door" pins the behaviour when the member is absent: the refusal stays the finding, with a note.
- **`HttpApp.installManaged`** — a new method on an exported class: RIGHT. It calls the same door as `installUnmanaged` (`POST /api/v1/marketplace/install-local`) with `installMode: 'managed'`. The door parses `installMode` against `InstallModeSchema`, where `managed` is a legal value (`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` around line 2476).
- **`installableManifest(artifact, mode = 'unmanaged')`** — a new optional parameter with a default: RIGHT. A call with one argument behaves as before; the two existing `units.test.ts` expectations are unchanged and still pass. With `'managed'` it adds no `installModes`. The door then reads the build's own declaration, and absent means `['managed']` (`resolveInstallModes`, around line 5035). A build that declares only `unmanaged` would be refused `INSTALL_MODE_NOT_PERMITTED`. That case lands in the "managed refused too" finding, which is handled and tested.
- **`fallsBackToManaged`** — a new export: RIGHT. Its body is `!refusal.ok && refusal.code === 'UNMANAGED_INSTALL_UNCOPYABLE'`.
  - It falls back on that one code only. It does not check the status, and the code alone is the right discriminator.
  - The code is registered in the spec error-code ledger (`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts:792`) and stamped as 422 by `unmanagedInstallUncopyable` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/package-unmanaged-install.ts:349`).
  - The fallback rightly does not trigger on the authoring-time sibling `STACK_UNMANAGED_INSTALL_UNCOPYABLE`.
  - The fallback runs only when `options.managedFallback === true`, and only `askMode` passes that.
  - Test case 2 pins that `INSTALL_MODE_NOT_PERMITTED` 422, `UNMANAGED_INSTALL_WALLED_POSTURE` 409 and `PLUGIN_MANIFEST_INVALID` 400 never reach the managed door.
- **`InstallAnswer`, `InstalledBuild`** — new exported types: RIGHT.
- **`ModeRun.template` retyped as `InstalledBuild`**: this narrows nothing. Field by field, `InstalledBuild` is the old inline type: `source: string`, `install` (`InstallAnswer` is the old inline `ok/status/code?/message?`), and `installModesSupplied: boolean`. It only adds two optional fields, `installMode?` and `unmanagedRefusal?`.
  - A reader keeps every field, with the same type and the same optionality.
  - A writer's existing object literals still type-check, because the added fields are optional.
  - Inside the package, the only readers (`summary.ts:264`, `scorecard.ts:673`, `cli.ts:370`) read `.source` alone.

**Run-record shape:** every template or ask install now writes `installMode`. A fallback also writes `unmanagedRefusal`. Older records have no `installMode`, and the jsdoc says those installed unmanaged. That is an additive output change, and the Clause-② line declares it: RIGHT.

**Behaviour:**

- **Ask mode on `UNMANAGED_INSTALL_UNCOPYABLE`**: RIGHT. It installs the same build managed, minus only the `installModes: ['unmanaged']` the runner itself adds. Nothing is stripped, and test case 1 pins that `capabilities` is kept. This is the seat's option A from the claim note. Options B and C are not taken.
- **Fresh copies**: RIGHT. A copy installs the way the run's own install landed (`landed`). Test case 1 pins that a copy never calls the unmanaged door after a fallback.
- **Template mode**: never falls back. Its refusal stays the finding and the iterate does not run (test case 4). Its record now also carries `installMode: 'unmanaged'`.
- **Managed refused too**: one finding names both answers. The template keeps `installMode: 'managed'` and `unmanagedRefusal` (test case 5).

**Is the install mode unmistakable in a round record?** Yes, at the record and scorecard level.

- The JSON record carries `template.installMode` on every new install, and `template.unmanagedRefusal` on a fallback.
- The rendered scorecard prints `- ask finding: unmanaged install refused UNMANAGED_INSTALL_UNCOPYABLE (422): installed the same build managed instead` (`scorecard.ts:881`; test case 1 pins the rendered line).
- The fallback also shows in the live-proof scorecard.

The cross-run `summary` table neither shows install mode nor refuses to mix it: it is not in `TABLE_DIMENSIONS` and not in the `suppliedAxis` row key. Two install modes cannot share one cell unknowingly, for three reasons:

1. The row key pins the build: the template's sha256, or the scratch build's author.
2. The `package source` dimension pins the platform.
3. The refusal is a static classification of the build's keys (`UNMANAGED_INSTALL_KEY_DISPOSITIONS`), so one build on one platform lands the same mode on every run. A record from before this PR could not supply a cell for a refused build, because such a run ran zero turns.

A reader who compares rows or cards in a summary still sees no install-mode label (N1).

**Live proof** (travel_expense, template sha256 `b7ab31a7…`, ask mode, `--ask-repeats 1`, published 18.5.0, subscription login):

- The unmanaged install was refused 422 `UNMANAGED_INSTALL_UNCOPYABLE`, and the managed install answered 200.
- 13 question turns and 6 operations ran, against 0 in the refused round.
- The proof ran at `264f86d2`. I read `264f86d2..18bbea25` in full. It changes behaviour in no way:
  - The `MANAGED_FALLBACK_CODE` constant becomes the inline `fallsBackToManaged` comparison.
  - The finding and refusal strings now take `install.code` where they took the constant, which is the same value on this branch.
  - The added `!ok` is redundant inside `if (!install.ok)`.
- The seed loaded 173 of 757 rows, as the PR's acceptance note says. The scratch run of the same build loaded the same 173 of 757, so that comes from the build, not from the managed install.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/34687-ask-managed-install.md` gives `'@objectstack/scenarios': patch`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- AGENTS.md workflow §3: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`, and kind `none` takes `patch`. The level is RIGHT.
- Nothing a metadata author can write changes. The diff touches only the eval runner, so `none` is RIGHT.
- The Clause-② enumeration is complete against the diff: `AppHarness.installManaged`, `HttpApp.installManaged`, the `mode` parameter, `fallsBackToManaged`, `InstalledBuild`, `InstallAnswer`, and `ModeRun.template` with its two optional fields. The new helper `installAnswerOf` is not exported, so it is rightly not counted.
- The PR-body and changeset `Clause-②:` lines are byte-identical (`cmp`).
- The `(widening)` arm is right: nothing is removed, retyped narrower or made required. No ADR-0087 disposition is owed.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — confirmed. It is optional and backward compatible for existing implementers of `AppHarness`, callers of `installableManifest`, and readers or writers of `ModeRun.template`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`**: `[]`. Nothing to answer.
- **Dev deviation (1)**: the pins go in the shared harness file `test/runner/orchestrate.test.ts`, not a new card-named file. Accepted: AGENTS.md (ruling record 6583487846) puts a new pin in the component's existing harness file.
- **Dev deviation (2)**: the PR body ends with a plain-text `signed:` line, not an HTML comment. Accepted: os-dev.md bars dev-written HTML comments. This is cosmetic and touches no contract.
- **Dev deviation (3)**: the platform code is compared inline, not declared as a runner constant, so that `check:error-code-provenance` does not read `@objectstack/scenarios` as a stamp site. Accepted. The runner stamps nothing; `metadata-protocol` owns the code, and a comparison is not a stamp site under that gate. A renamed code would not fail silently: the old code would stop falling back, and the refusal would surface as the mode's finding with its code.
- **`out_of_scope_findings`**: none.
- **`security_findings`**: none. A managed install of a supplied build is what the platform itself prescribes for this refusal. It goes through the same admin-session door, and no new credential or route is introduced.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5)**: not applicable, no finding. The diff makes HTTP calls to the install door in an eval runner. It adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

**Findings**

- **N1 (nit)**: the summary table's ask rows do not label the install mode. The mode is pinned implicitly by the build sha256 and the package source (see ①), so no cell can mix modes. Still, a row label such as `· installed managed` would make the difference explicit when a reader compares rows or cards. This affects neither correctness nor the contract.
- **N2 (nit)**: the jsdoc on `InstallAnswer` reads "A refused install, as the door answered it." The type also holds accepted answers (`template.install` `{ ok: true, status: 200 }`). Suggested: "An install, as the door answered it."
- **N3 (nit)**: in the PR body's Ablation section, the first leg's anchor (`if (!options.managedFallback || install.code !== … || installManaged === undefined) {`) is the `264f86d2` text, not the head's. That leg ran before the last commit. The last commit changes no behaviour, and the same five cases pass at the head (the 1057-test package run), so this is an evidence-currency nit only.

No S item is open, only nits, so this meets the merge standard.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-34687-ask-managed-install`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgh1zkZzDXL36ckWAG`

**VERDICT: PASS**
